      6. Measurable functions#

      In this section we investigate when a function is compatible with an algebra structure defined on its domain and codomain.

      For a function and define If and carry -algebras, measurability requires every measurable set in the target space to pull back to a measurable set in the domain.

      After studying these notes, you will be able to do the following.

      • Verify measurability by testing inverse images of a generating family.

      • Construct pullback, product, and trace -algebras.

      • Apply level-set criteria to real- and extended-real-valued functions.

      • Prove that measurable functions remain measurable under pasting, algebraic operations, lattice operations, and pointwise limits when the operations are defined.

      6.1.3 Borel and Lebesgue measurability#

      For a topological space , write for the -algebra generated by the open subsets of .

      Theorem 11 (Continuous maps are Borel measurable)#

      Let and be topological spaces. Every continuous map is measurable.

      Proof#

      The generator criterion reduces the claim to inverse images of open sets. The open subsets of generate . If is open, continuity gives that is open in , and hence . Apply Proposition 5.

      Definition 12 (Borel and Lebesgue measurable functions)#

      A function is

      1. Borel measurable if it is -measurable;

      2. Lebesgue measurable if it is -measurable, where is the Lebesgue -algebra.

      Since , every Borel measurable real-valued function on is Lebesgue measurable. Careful, the converse does not hold (since the inclusion is actually strict)!
